Instrument (EN): Professional Identity Questionnaire — validated Persian nursing-student adaptation
Scales / measured domains (EN): Two correlated dimensions: Professional Identity Formation—Attachment (PIF-A); Professional Identity Formation—Detachment (PIF-D, reverse-scored); total professional identity score 10–50. This PIQ is not the PSIQ-9 professional self-identity questionnaire.
Research provenance: Sefidkar R, Kermani M, Keshmiri F, BMC Nursing, published 2026-10-13, DOI 10.1186/s12912-026-05497-9. Beaton-guided Persian translation/cultural adaptation; CFA N226 undergraduate Iranian nursing students, test-retest independent student sample N100 (ICC .79, 95% CI .71–.85). Separate N110 early-career nurses was exploratory descriptive/associational application, not an additional validation cohort. Alpha total .86, PIF-A .93, PIF-D .78, CFA CFI .99, RMSEA .01; loadings .30–.90.
DB locales: No corresponding PIQ-10 family/key in 3919 Master, 11_DB_Registered, PR#495 386-source index or published Supabase 149 keys; independent FA-IR validation recorded, NOT DB-active.
EN form: English-named earlier PIQ instrument; do not assume a separately validated EN respondent-language version from publication language or transfer Iran norms to English.
RU form: No validated Russian PIQ-10 questionnaire verified.
ES form: No validated Spanish PIQ-10 questionnaire verified.
Other translations: FA-IR: explicitly translated, culturally adapted and psychometrically evaluated Persian respondent form in Iranian nursing-student sample N226; distinct N100 test-retest. No claim of validation in all Persian-speaking settings.
Target population: Iranian undergraduate nursing students (CFA N226 and separate retest N100), plus early-career nursing cohort N110 for descriptive exploratory application only; no general-adult, therapist or clinical diagnostic validity.

PIF-D reverse scoring; 110-nurse sample NOT independent psychometric validation. No test publication/clinical or workforce decisions.

Instrument (EN): Unbearable Psychache Scale — independently studied Italian 3-item edition
Scales / measured domains (EN): One unidimensional domain: intolerable/unbearable psychological pain (psychache); brief subscale adapted from longer Psychache Scale (PAS-13). NOT a stand-alone suicide risk classifier.
Research provenance: Bungaro N et al., Frontiers in Psychology, published 2025-11-04, DOI 10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1676675. Two separate Italian community adult samples: N707 Study1 single-factor confirmatory fit and consistency (alpha .905); N257 Study2 convergent and ROC investigations (alpha .929). Recent suicide-risk ROC AUC approximately .75–.83; recent suicidal behavior PPV only .21 and recent suicidal ideation PPV .42; no incremental predictive value over PAS13.
DB locales: No UP3/PAS-3 key in 3919 Master, 11_DB_Registered, PR#495 386-source index or Supabase published 149 keys. Research only; no live clinical use.
EN form: UP3 original developed by Pachkowski et al. 2019 from English PAS13; article language/earlier original do not establish a newly validated translated EN form in this cycle.
RU form: No independently validated Russian UP3 questionnaire verified.
ES form: No independently validated Spanish UP3 questionnaire verified.
Other translations: IT-IT: Italian UP3 participant-language edition psychometrically evaluated in two independent Italian adult community samples N707+N257; no transfer of Italy-specific risk accuracy to other languages or populations.
Target population: Community-recruited Italian adults; predominantly women, Study1 N707 mean age ~30.7, Study2 N257 mean age ~31.8; no independent clinic-based prospective diagnostic validation.
Commercial digital use / permission revi: Frontiers article CC BY may permit article reuse but does not demonstrate third-party ownership or commercial reuse licence for PAS13-derived item wording, translated question texts or scored clinical SaaS. Obtain permission from original PAS/UP3 rights owners and Italian adaptation authors; require licensed questionnaire and detailed safety/clinical governance.
Validated edition evidence / links: https://doi.org/10.3389/fpsyg.2025.1676675 ; UP3 original Pachkowski et al. (2019) cited in primary paper
Verification notes / safety gate: RESEARCH_ONLY / CLINICIAN_ONLY / RIGHTS NOT CLEARED. Self-reported psychache cannot diagnose suicidal risk; AUC not sufficient for autonomous triage, low PPV for behaviors .21, no incremental validity over PAS13. Do NOT host items, cutoffs, clinical risk scores, or automated crisis decisions.
